changes.ink: There is a distinct dark glyph between the small x and the comparison sign, with a short sloping upper stroke and two tight lower bends. Its presence is certain; its identity and any revision history are not. H omits that ink.
The opening and closing marks are high paired short strokes, not angular guillemets.
The first short group is en, followed by c/o/m and a descending p in composant, with a final tall t. It does not have the letter sequence morphisme.
The et is ordinary baseline ink. The long curved line to its left is the leader of soit d, and does not strike through et.

changes.place: First word of the upper cancellation
changes.ink: The short cancelled group exposes the initial d and a short low ending; there is no independently exposed long ons run. Dire remains tentative because the horizontal strike covers bodies.
The d and apostrophe are visible, followed by a compressed low run and an ending point. The run is compatible with ens. but is partly covered, so its letters remain locally doubtful.

changes.place: Upper cancellation: ordonnés versus H’s ending and comma
changes.ink: The low word begins with the exposed o/r/d shapes, while the remaining bodies and ending intersect the strike and inserted line. The ending and H’s comma are not securely settled; no substantive H error is counted for this unresolved local reading.
The first group is the short on form. Suppose has its two descending p strokes and a short final e; there is no final ant/t sequence.
The final accented e closes the word before déjà; no further e body is written.
A separate d and apostrophe precede the low avance run. The word is not dimension.
The replacement occupies the raised line between the two struck baselines of the old sentence. H runs it into the old wording without representing this complete replacement as an insertion.
There are two separated short word groups, the low on stroke and the small a; no tall l or remaining alors letters appear. Both adjacent comparison signs are plainly less-than signs.
After on the source has the short se followed by a tall b and the low orne run; it does not repeat the opening s’intéresse.
After the visible p/l/o/n/g sequence the writing goes directly to the short t/s ending, with no ement run. The first C candidate is resolved, but no substantive C error is counted.
The far-right word has the tall f and compressed onc/t/s ending; the expanded ions sequence is absent. The visible short form is retained.
The low final m ends before a clear gap and sur; there is no separate dark point in that gap.

changes.place: Long cancellation: possible ce before qui
changes.ink: Small curved ink at the opening parenthesis is compatible with ce but is crowded and weak. Its reading remains open; H’s omission of ce is not counted as a proved error.

The adjective is at the right edge and crossed by a diagonal stroke. The first run is compatible with maximale, but the middle letters and ending do not securely exclude minimale. H’s candidate remains admitted and is not counted as a substantive error.

A separate older horizontal cancellation crosses the small q-descender group and following short group before soit. This is actual ink inside the later paragraph cancellation. The provisional words qui est remain doubtful.
Between pour and the parameter the short tout is visible, with its t strokes and low middle bodies. H has no corresponding word.

changes.place: Parameter in the raised condition: unresolved collation
changes.ink: The heavily retraced parameter has a low tail and a dense loop; this first occurrence can also look like p. The membership sign, double-stem N and star are clear. H’s p remains an admitted alternative, so this open collation is excluded from substantive error counts.
After the tall h the word ends with one accented e; there is no second e before à D.
The abbreviation ends with a low m and a blank interval before the retraced parameter. No separate dark point follows codim. The full stop after the parameter is retained.

The loop lies to the left of a high stem, and a lower tail is also present. These give competing d-like and q-like forms, without a recoverable revision sequence. The parameter is not settled across its three occurrences, and no definitive H symbol error is counted.
After the struck older word the live sequence is v/o/i/t: a small v, rounded o, dotted i and tall t. There is no initial écr sequence. Aisément is legible after it.
The small bien is written in the interline below the target baseline, after ce sont and before là. Its looped b and short ien run are clear.
Que is at the end of the upper line; the next line begins the descending j of je and the low note with its final tall t. The source does not have prolonge.

The subscript has the same crowded closed loop, high stem and lower curled tail seen in the preceding parameter, with additional retracing. Identity and sequence of rewriting remain unresolved. H’s definite p is recorded as an alternative, not counted as a proved symbol error.
The pale lower-left figures are a slanting 1, closed 0 and looped 6. There is no dark authorial page number at the head of this sheet.

decisions.ink: The extra two-bend glyph is definite ink; xi is only a provisional identity. No independent cancellation stroke or earlier glyph can be separated.
The first function letter has overlapping rounded and upright strokes. The current letter and any prior letter cannot be ordered reliably; the following c(y) is clear.
The short ts ending follows the descending g directly; no ement bodies are present.
Tall f plus compressed oncts run at the right edge; no expanded ions ending.
The first parameter has a dense head and lower tail, with a p-like right loop also possible. The other occurrences do not reveal a secure revision chronology.
Two retraced oblique strokes meet at a lower point, making a capital V; no separate older letter or deletion is identifiable.
The high stem supports d while the lower curled tail supports q; the dark overlapping loop does not settle which form is current.
The D subscript repeats the crowded high stem, closed loop and lower tail; no reliable order of strokes establishes a final q or d.

notes: There is no dark authorial page number at the head. The pale lower-left 106 is recorded separately from the digital scan number 107, without identifying the foliation hand.

The page begins with an ordered set J and embeddings into the displayed Delta expression, defines or assumes a codimension function, and then restricts to compatible ordered embeddings. It next cancels an assumption about a least element and starts describing pairs (x,V) and an analytic multiplicity. These are statements of the manuscript, not a proof of its analytic construction.

The extra xi-like mark in 150 is real ink and is preserved. The hook and two right-arrowhead branches, the phi label, Delta subscript x, comparison sign, P(I(x)) and upper circle were all inspected together. No definite earlier cancelled glyph is inferred from the retracing.
The calligraphic P follows C’s supplied notation convention. Its difference from H’s mathfrak P is not counted as a proved alphabet error from the handwritten P outline alone.

The live text is en composant, followed by the small soit d, insertion, then live et. The second raised line reads on suppose donné déjà d d’avance sur J. Its repeated déjà/d’avance wording is retained literally.

In 151 both comparison signs point left and are strict less-than signs. The words are on a, and the second function letter is c. The first d/c is heavily retraced and remains unresolved; no independent cancelled earlier letter is reconstructed.

Conditional local mathematical comparison, performed by the main reader: in a two-branch coordinate model, the germ {z1=z2=0} is strictly contained in {z1=0}, but their ambient codimensions are 2 and 1 respectively. If Delta is ordered by germ inclusion and the function in 151 is this codimension, strict inclusion makes it decrease, contrary to the displayed increasing less-than relation. This is conditional on those interpretations, retains the unresolved first d/c, and does not prove or refute the page’s global analytic construction. All written signs remain unchanged.
The short forms plongts, foncts and codim are retained without expansion or an added point after the two live codim occurrences. The separate codim. inside the cancelled paragraph does have a point.

The whole paragraph beginning On suppose de plus is cancelled, including the opening assertion. Three long diagonal strokes and six short left boundary strokes indicate its scope; they are recorded as cancellation geometry, not as a separate unrelated illustration. The older horizontal deletion qui est lies within that later cancellation and is separately represented.

Local cancellation doubts are retained on dire, ens., ordonnés, the retraced a, ce, maximale|minimale, qui est and the older voit. The added doubts are certainty changes, not substantive errors against C. No hidden letters have been supplied from grammatical expectations.

The three parameter forms have been compared on their own crops. The first can resemble p, while the later two have both a d-like high stem and a q-like lower tail. Their source identity and any rewriting chronology remain unresolved. H’s p is explicitly retained among the apparatus alternatives, so the three open parameter rows are excluded from substantive H error counts pending further reading.

The tuple has a clearly retraced V with a downward point; a plain V occurs again in the following line. No earlier letter is reconstructed. The source attaché ends in a single accented e, which is retained without grammatical normalization.

The source has a cancelled older voit followed by live voit aisément. Bien is interlinear below the target baseline and attaches before là. The final naming words are que je note, followed by D with the doubtful parameter subscript; the page ends on et on a un morphisme without completing that morphism here.

M1161, M1162 and M1164 resolve to C’s first readings plongts, foncts and V. These resolutions alone are excluded from substantive C error counts. M1159, M1160, M1163, M1165 and M1166 remain unresolved.

The original and the two native halves were each viewed once. Twelve local crops were created once and each actually viewed; the main reader also independently viewed the original and all twelve crops. There was no OCR, external research, new first-pass crop, TeX compilation or blind reading.
The count is 27 written baselines: 23 main baselines including the two numbered display rows, plus four interlinear insertion rows. The isolated pale foliation is inventoried separately and excluded.

check_events.outcome: Main reader checked the conditional two-branch example: {z1=z2=0} is strictly included in {z1=0}, while their ambient codimensions are 2 and 1. Therefore germ-inclusion order together with this codimension would reverse, rather than satisfy, the written increasing relation in 151. This is only a conditional local comparison; the ink, first d/c uncertainty and global analytic construction are not repaired or claimed proved.
